parsed.attack: The nearest thing in the graveyard is Tandem's live fitness product [46], whose founders concluded that live, scheduled, human-delivered practice "isn't that engaging" and that the supply side would not adopt a new platform - the same hourly-human model this replaces. The secondary graveyard risk is the consumable-credit shape: a naturalization interview happens once in a lifetime, so there is no second purchase and lifetime revenue is roughly whatever the first pack costs, which is the structure that buried most one-off exam-prep apps against a $20-$80 cost per paying user.
parsed.strongest_defence: Every close predecessor died because a person had to be scheduled, show up and be paid by the hour; unscripted speech-to-speech at half a cent to two cents a minute removes that supply side entirely, and the free-to-paid step is a twelve-minute mock the week before a dated government appointment, which is as acute as consumer urgency gets.
parsed.verdict_reason: No close predecessor died of anything other than the cost and scheduling of a human tutor, and that cause is genuinely dissolved by a named capability change in real-time voice pricing.
